name: lab_state
description: Read a network-xray lab state (read-only) and summarize it. Starts with `wrong`: what is wrong, each with a `text` line (an interface down, an OSPF interface that faces a neighbor and has no adjacency with the values both ends must share and do not, a Full adjacency whose ends still differ, a BGP session not Established); empty when nothing is. Then nodes and interfaces, links, OSPF adjacencies, BGP sessions and counts. An adjacency that never came up is not in a neighbor table, so counts also has ospf_ifaces_expected (OSPF interfaces that face a neighbor, not passive), ospf_ifaces_full and ospf_ifaces_without_adjacency. No router is contacted.

path.description: A state_<node>.json, a directory of them, an xray-states.js, or a directory of saved FRR show ... json files

name: why_best_path
description: For one node and prefix, give the BGP best path and the reason stored in the data (FRR selectionReason, or the IOS-XE collector's derived reason). If the data has no reason, reason is null and a note says so; nothing is guessed. Read-only.

prefix.description: Prefix, e.g. 8.8.8.0/24 (the length may be omitted when unambiguous)

vrf.description: VRF, only needed when the prefix is in several VRFs

name: list_routers
description: List the routers in a network-xray lab state and which protocols have state for each (ospf: OSPF neighbors or LSDB in the data; bgp: BGP neighbors or BGP routes), whether a routing table was collected, and row counts. Read-only.

name: ospf_neighbors
description: Starts with `wrong`: what is wrong, for OSPF and interfaces, each with a `text` line (an interface down, an OSPF interface that faces a neighbor and has no adjacency with the values both ends must share and do not, a Full adjacency whose ends still differ); empty when nothing is. Then OSPF neighbors per router as collected: neighbor router ID, address, state (e.g. Full), interface, and DR/BDR role and peer node name when known. All routers, or one with `router`. Read-only.

router.description: Only this router, e.g. r1 (default: all routers)

name: ospf_interfaces
description: Starts with `wrong`: what is wrong, for OSPF and interfaces, each with a `text` line (an interface down, an OSPF interface that faces a neighbor and has no adjacency with the values both ends must share and do not, a Full adjacency whose ends still differ); empty when nothing is. Then `mismatches` and `hints` (below), then the OSPF interface values per router as collected: MTU, hello and dead intervals, network type, area, cost, DR/BDR role, priority, passive, authentication (none / simple / md5) and neighbor counts. For a link it also gives the other end and `mismatches`: one line per value that must be equal for an adjacency but is not, e.g. "r1 eth1 MTU 1500 ⇔ r2 eth1 MTU 1400". A value the router did not report is null and is not compared; each interface also has the neighbor state there, and `hints` names a link stuck in ExStart / Exchange whose MTU was not reported. All routers, or one with `router`. Read-only.

router.description: Only this router, e.g. r1 (default: all routers)

name: bgp_neighbors
description: Starts with `wrong`: each BGP session that is not Established, with a `text` line (empty when none). Then BGP neighbors per router as collected: peer address, remote AS, iBGP/eBGP, state, established, and prefixes received (null when the data has no count). All routers, or one with `router`. Read-only.

router.description: Only this router, e.g. r1 (default: all routers)

name: route_lookup
description: Look up a destination address in one router's collected routing table (installed rows only) by longest prefix match: the matching route, its protocol, next hop and outgoing interface (all next hops for ECMP). next_hop is null for a directly connected route; route is null with a note when nothing matches. A recursive next hop carries resolved_via (what the router resolved it through; via_mgmt when that is the lab's management network, i.e. not reachable inside the lab topology) and a note says so. This reads the table the collector saved; it does not compute routing. Read-only.

destination.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address, e.g. 8.8.8.8 or 2001:db8::1 (no prefix length)

vrf.description: VRF of the routing table rows to search (default: the default VRF)

name: why_path
description: Why one router selected its BGP path to a prefix: the selected path, the other candidates with their attributes, the deciding step, and where that reason came from: reason_source "device" when the router reported it (FRR selectionReason), "derived" when the collector worked it out from what the router printed (Cisco IOS-XE prints no reason), "comparison" when network-xray inferred it by comparing the attributes in the data (Weight, LocPrf, AS-Path, Origin, MED), or null with a note when neither says. A bare address is matched to the longest BGP prefix that contains it. Read-only.

prefix.description: Prefix (e.g. 8.8.8.0/24) or an address inside it (e.g. 8.8.8.8)

vrf.description: VRF, only needed when the prefix is in several VRFs

name: state_diff
description: What changed from a baseline state you kept to the state now, heaviest first: routers gone or not read, interfaces down, OSPF adjacencies lost, OSPF interface values both ends must share that changed, BGP sessions down, best paths that moved (with the router's reason), routes removed or moved (with originated_by: the router where that prefix is directly connected), then what came back or was added. none is true when nothing changed. Uptimes, counters and the management network are not compared. The baseline is whatever path you pass as before (a state you saved, or collect's previous). Read-only.

before.description: The baseline state (same input as lab_state)

after.description: The state now (same input as lab_state)
